a study on human nature and desire

by hybriade

Summary

Mydei comes to learn two startling truths of the world.

One—someone up there really hates him.

Two—he’s not a bull. He’s a cow. A dairy cow.

And he needs to be milked.

Cipher plays a prank that causes everyone in Okhema to sprout animal features.

Mydei, much to his dismay, ends up as a dairy cow.

“Lady Cipher, what are you doing?” Castorice asks. 

Cipher pauses, having been in the middle of pouring some strange shimmering substance into the city’s water supply. She looks over and gives a wide grin, showing off sharp fangs. “Princess Homebody! Nice to see you here!” 

Castorice stares at the bottle in Cipher’s hands then back up at her. “Uh…” 

“The month of Fortune begins tomorrow!” Cipher explains with a wink as she empties out the rest of the liquid and tosses the bottle to the side. “We’re starting off with a bang! Just some good harmless fun, that’s all!”

“Right…” Castorice’s eyebrows pinch as she wrings her hands together. “Has Lady Aglaea approved this?” 

“What kind of question is that?” Cipher asks, pulling her arms behind her head as she leisurely makes her way to Castorice, hips swaying side to side. 

“I’m guessing that’s a no…” Castorice murmurs, only to squeak when Cipher leans forwards, promptly jumping back to maintain her designated distance.

“Say, Princess Homebody, what do you think of human nature?” 

“Eh?” Castorice’s eyes widen. “W-What do you mean?”

“Hm, let’s say we have a guy who’s known to be a lover of chimeras. He’s always seen with his friends visiting the garden of life, playing with the chimeras and bringing them treats, but turns out, he actually prefers dromases! What do you think of him?”

“He’s not true to himself…? He’s looking to fit in with his friends?”

“Correct! Two points to Princess Homebody!” Cipher places a thoughtful hand to her chin and continues, “People play the part in public. They act in fabricated manners, control their speech and attitudes, whilst constantly lying to themselves that they aren’t the sum of their darkest desires… They hide their true selves behind a mask—a fortress of lies—and will never allow it to fall, even when surrounded by loved ones and friends. Relationships are built on burying the truest parts of ourselves, hiding away the vices that lay within and make us who we are. Such is the truth of human nature and the source of many a conflict.”

Castorice nods, following along. “So, what you’re saying is—” 

“Everyone in Okhema will wake up with animal features like little old me!” 

“... Oh.” 

“C’mon, give me a little more!” Cipher exclaims, placing a hand to her heart and sniffling.  

“Lady Cipher, I don’t mean to offend, but I don’t think this is a good idea…”

“Aw, don’t say that! Aren’t you the least bit curious?” 

Cipher claps her hands together, kaleidoscope eyes curving into crescents as she circles around Castorice like a prowling cat surrounding wounded prey. “What animal someone presents as will reveal a lot about their internal character. I find it rather intriguing.” 

The conflict remains. Castorice’s delicate features stay scrunched, and she begins to tug at the butterflies decorating her arms. 

“I wonder what you’d be,” Cipher ponders. “Perhaps a bunny. Floppy ears. Poofy tail. Easy to startle. Cute.” 

At once, Castorice’s cheeks flush bright red, and the poor decorative butterfly is crushed beneath her grip. She wraps her arms around herself as if to shield. 

Cipher continues on, “So, what animal do you think that rascal Phainon would be?” 

Castorice pauses. Thinks about it. Slowly, she says, “A puppy… or an oryx.”

“Oryx? That’s a little specific, don’t you think?” 

The shift is immediate. 

Like a wilted plant given water, Castorice perks up. All wariness is wiped, and she gives an overly enthusiastic nod before pulling out a frilly purple notebook and flipping to a random page. A glint to her amethyst eyes, she taps deftly against a diagram and begins speaking like a conspiracy theorist. “There are many, many reasons as to why I believe Lord Phainon will present as an oryx! First, let me start off with a little background. So, what is an oryx and how does it connect to Lord Phainon, you ask? Let me explain!”

In one breath, Castorice launches into a whole tirade, pointing to specific portions of her diagram and changing topics every few seconds. Her shy features are lit up like the searing rays from the towering dawn device. 

Cipher stares. Silent. For once in her life, she has nothing to say, but she is impressed. She stands there, dumbfounded by the sudden switch in roles, as Castorice continues on and on. 

Something about looks being deceiving? Oryx matching lions even though they’re herbivores? Phainon being too kind for his own good? 

With a deep inhale, Castorice slams her notebook shut and concludes, “In summary, Lord Phainon is an oryx because he’s sweet and gentle, but those horns pack a nasty punch.”

“Sweet and gentle?” Cipher questions, arms crossed against her chest as she rolls her eyes. “Yeah, right…” 

“I say that in jest,” Castorice giggles. “Who knows what he’s actually like when he’s not helping old ladies cross the road.”  

“How about the little lion—prince?” 

Castorice tilts her head. “You answered your own question.” 

“Touché.” 

“I can envision cat too,” Castorice muses. “But lions are cats so I guess it’s in the same vein…”

Knock! Knock! Knock! 

Mydei groans and shifts in bed, yanking his blanket over himself and curling up into a tight ball. 

He’s tired. It’s been a long week of fighting off rabid titankin and dealing with a certain moonlight-haired Deliverer forcefully dragging him off to the baths in the middle of the night with little rhyme or reason. There’s little use in trying to elucidate the strange happenings in that giant head. 

Unfortunately, even Mydei’s overwhelming sleepiness can’t abate the knowledge that, yes, of course it’s who he thinks it is. Only one person in all of Amphoreus has the audacity to march up to his door and knock like he owns the place. One stupidly infuriating man with too bright of a smile and a knack for causing a ruckus. 

Another knock, and Mydei mourns his early losses. 

“Mydei! Mydei, wake up! Hey! I’m going to keep yelling until you open the door! It’s already the third quint of entry hour! How are you still asleep?” 

Shut up. Mydei bites his lip. Phainon’s boisterous voice, while already excessively loud, is somehow even more grating than usual. He didn’t even think it was possible, but Okhema’s golden boy always exceeds his expectations in one way or another. 

And he’s persistent too. Perseverance is a necessity for being a good warrior but this isn’t the battlefield. There’s a time and place for everything, but not now. 

As a last ditch effort, Mydei clutches onto his pillow and presses the sides against his ears. It does nothing. No, he still hears Phainon loud and clear. Something moves behind his back, fur brushing against his bare leg, but he makes little note of it. 

“Open up!” Phainon yells. “Mydei! Mydeimos! Crown prince of Castrum Kremnos! Please!”

Fuck it. He gives up and stomps out of bed, uncaring that his hair is a mangled mess and that he’s clothed in little more than his thin night robes. He’s about to yank his front door wide open and give the Deliverer a piece of his mind when he hears, “Everyone in Okhema has animal ears! I just saw Krateros. He’s an badger! Can you believe that?” 

Animal ears…? Did he hear that correctly?

He swings the door open to find Phainon, grinning from ear to ear, only his humans ears are gone. Instead, large wolf ears adorn his head, snowy white and looking irresistibly soft. He even sees one of them twitch, and the urge to reach out and pet them is overwhelming. And is that a fluffy tail he sees?

Mydei blinks. Rubs his eyes a few times. The ears and tails remain. What in the Nikador is going on?

The smile drops off Phainon’s face, and his tail, once lively, stiffens, sticking straight up as if reaching for the sky. Mydei tilts his head, confused by the sudden change. 

“You’re a…” Phainon swallows. He waves his arms around. Coughs a little. A lot. Swallows again. All in the span of a few seconds. He looks almost frightened? Concerned? Maybe a bit of  confusion too. It’s like he’s been dunked into a cold bath and then slapped in the face right after. 

“Deliverer—” 

“Bull…” Phainon finishes. He frowns. “Or cow?” He looks down to Mydei’s chest and mutters, “Cow. Definitely cow.” 

“...” Mydei’s gaze drops down to his chest. Now that he mentions it, his pecs do feel more tender than usual. Maybe a little fuller too. There’s a strange weightiness to them that hadn’t existed before, but he chalks it up to being tired. 

This is all some strange dream he’s concocted. When he wakes up for real, he’ll probably go hide in the corner of his bathroom and debate his life choices. 

“Come again?” 

“You’re a cow,” Phainon says. “Like, y’know… the animal where we get milk from… Big udders…”

“I’m a bull,” Mydei deadpans, playing along with whatever farce is going on. Rationally, he’s sure there’s a reason for all this madness, but he’s too afraid to look at himself in the mirror to find out. And besides, if he did have ears and a tail, there’s no way he would be a cow of all animals. It’s preposterous. He’s been compared to a lion more times than he could count. He’s practically synonymous with lion. There’s no way he’s a—

Phainon reaches out to yank Mydei’s new ears, and Mydei nearly slams the door on Phainon’s arm. 

“I thought you would have been a lion. Small little lion ears and all, but this is cute too. Unexpected, but cute,” Phainon laughs as he plays around with Mydei’s ears. His blue eyes twinkle, and his usual sunshine smile brightens his handsome features. Only now, his canines have sharpened into glistening fangs, and Mydei feels a rush of adrenaline roll down his spine. 

No, he’s not scared. Just a little surprised. That’s all. The goosebumps on his body are only because it’s cold outside. Never mind the hundred degree weather. 

Also, did Phainon just call him cute? Of all things, cute? Seriously?

“Do you have a death wish?” Mydei asks. He crosses his arms against his chest and tilts his head upwards in his usual arrogant fashion.

“Not particularly.” Unbothered, Phainon continues toying with Mydei’s ear, rolling his finger over the shell and tracing over the dark spots. “Can’t blame me for calling you cute when you’re turning red, Mydei.” 

“I’m not—” He stops. Turns even redder. He’s sure his face is the same color as the crimson markings that adorn his body. 

He also feels slightly akin to injured prey being toyed with by a sadistic predator, which is dumb and irrational but so is whatever this whole situation is. Is he dreaming? He better be. 

“You’re testing me today, Deliverer,” Mydei says, ears flicking in annoyance as he bats Phainon’s hand away. He aims for a scary glare, but Phainon only laughs as if he’s been told a witty joke. 

Infuriating. 

“Don’t I always?” Phainon sighs. “You’re hard to please, my dear prince.” His fluffy white tail wags behind him. 

Mydei’s eye twitches. He yanks Phainon by the collar and drags him in. 

“Eh?”

“You were crowding outside my door.” He points to the living room kline and says, “Sit down.” 

Phainon does as he’s told—sits on the kline and waits like an eager puppy awaiting instructions from its owner. His tail continues to wag and his ears, those accursed fluffy ears, twitch and flick at random. 

Mydei steps in front of Phainon, opens his mouth, and blurts out, “You’re a wolf.”

Very insightful. Good job Mydei. 

“Mmm, yes.” Phainon stares up. His lips are parted and those sharp, gleaming fangs taunt him. Briefly, he wonders how they would feel lodged in his neck. 

These newly found prey instincts—if that’s what this madness is—aren’t doing him any favors. Fighting against the growing urge to flee, Mydei continues, “I thought you’d be a bunny or maybe even a sheep.” 

To be frank, the first animal he thought of was a puppy, but puppies are dogs and wolves are dogs, so he doesn’t voice it. And all things considered, he’s a little miffed, not going to lie. 

Phainon blinks with those giant blue eyes of his, looking sweet and innocent as ever, even with the giant and rather menacing ears twitching atop his head. “Really now? No clue, if you’re insulting me or complimenting me. I, for one, am not too surprised by my outcome. You, on the other hand…” A shaky smile. “ It’s a surprise for sure but it’s also welcome... Those ears suit you more than I thought! You look good… I mean—You always do, but uh, it’s different this time?” 

Mydei reaches out. Those fluffy ears twitch beneath his touch. His fur is softer than even the pampered chimeras at the garden of life, like he’s touching a cloud. He can’t even bring himself to be surprised. After all, Phainon is sunshine incarnate. 

He’s always been weak to cute animals, and Phainon, by all means, fits that category. An adorable canine with sharp teeth that could easily rip his throat out, but an adorable canine nonetheless. 

Phainon even has the audacity to start whining like a needy puppy, causing Mydei to startle and nearly drop his hand only for Phainon to nuzzle into his touch. He looks up through thick lashes, no shame in his gaze, only a want—a desire for more. His tail thumps loudly behind him. 

“That feels good!” Phainon exclaims, shamelessly pushing his head against Mydei’s hand. “Don’t stop!”

This is a dream. It has to be. There’s no way this is real. 

Entranced, he continues to pet Phainon. 

—𖤓—

Turns out it’s not a dream. This is reality. 

Mydei stares at himself in the mirror. The bovine ears stare back at him. He pinches one in between his fingers and winces because he had forgotten that he still had his gauntlets on. Now, he’s bleeding a little. 

Okhema has been cursed. Well, more like the water supply has been tainted with, and it doesn’t take a detective to know who’s behind this. It’s an open secret. 

The calendar states bold and clear that today is the first day of the Month of Fortune, and there’s only one titan known for playing harmless yet infuriating tricks like this. Not a single soul is spared. At least the children are having a good time with their newfound ears and tails. 

Also, Phainon wasn’t lying about Krateros being a badger. He always thought his old mentor and fellow weathered warrior was more of a wolf than anything else but he also thought Phainon would be a bunny, so maybe he’s not the best person to ask when it comes to guessing who’s what animal. 

“What animal do you think Demetria is?” Phainon asks, arms behind his head, as they take their stroll through Marmoreal Market. Even with the strange situation at hand, the city remains bustling, as it always does. Business as usual. 

“The fruit stall vendor?”

“Yup! The one you always buy pomegranates from.” 

Mydei pauses to think. She sells fruit for a living and enjoys it. Unsurprisingly, the first animal that comes to mind is, “A fruit bat.” 

“Seriously?” Phainon raises an eyebrow. “That’s your guess?”

“She sells fruit. It’s the most rational choice, Deliverer.” 

Wrong. Turns out she’s a wombat. Honestly, he didn’t even know what a wombat was until now, yet Phainon had somehow guessed within the same marsupial family. 

“Tch. Ask me again,” Mydei says as they pass by the fruit stall and he’s struck in the face by how off he was. She does wave at him though, shouting that they’ve gotten a new batch of pomegranates, and Mydei can’t help but buy a bag. Maybe Phainon is right. She has him hooked. 

“Theodoros then. We’re getting close to his shop anyway.” 

Mydei takes a guess. The obvious answer would be an animal that likes fancy, shiny objects such as a ferret, but he had been wrong about Demetria. If he were to view Theodoros through a lens of character, then he would say a carefree man like him would be some type of dog. 

Surprise, surprise. He’s wrong again. Theodoros is indeed a ferret.

Phainon laughs at him, and Mydei fights the overwhelming urge to reach over yank Phainon’s fluffy tail until he whimpers. 

Is there any rhyme or reason to this? Doesn’t feel like there is, but he knows if he were to bring it up that he’d be mocked as a sore loser. 

He can admit though that walking through the city is quite the experience. There’s a plethora of animals—some he didn’t even know existed until now and some that have gone extinct ages ago. There’s even people presenting as chimeras! Oh, how he wishes that were him. 

There’s an elephant in the room, and it’s not the random Okheman soldier that walks by. He’s not going to mention the prying eyes and whispers, the gazes that land on his chest. Maybe he should cover up…  

When they step foot into the marble floors of the Hero’s Bath, he braces himself. Like a certified idiot, he had placed a bet with Phainon over what Aglaea and Tribbie would be. Winner takes all, and by all, he means if he loses he’ll be subject to Phainon’s whims for the day. Already, he can imagine himself pruning from spending too much time in the hot water of the baths. 

As it turns out, Aglaea is a ram with large curled horns that frame and highlight her radiant features while the triplets are hamsters with cute little speckled ears. He can’t say he’s surprised. The horns fit Aglaea, and his guess about the triplets being small rodents wasn’t too off.

It doesn’t quite help his mood when even Aglaea, the picture of serenity and grace, reacts when she sees him. She stills in her steps, arm hovering for a touch too long. 

“Aglaea, Lady Tribios,” Mydei greets, keeping his voice a careful neutral. He tries to remain calm, but his ears flap and flicker, and he can’t control it. It’s like they have a mind of their own, and it puts a dent in his whole steady even under stress persona that he likes to present. 

“De!” Tribbie greets with a wave of her small hands. “A cow, wow! It suits you really well!” 

Phainon snorts. Mydei glares. 

“I’m a bull,” Mydei says, crossing his arms over his chest, inadvertently squeezing his pecs together.   

“Are you sure about that?” Phainon mutters, not so subtly staring at Mydei’s round chest, only to promptly get elbowed. “Ow?! Mydei… That’s rude, you know!” 

“I see…” Aglaea murmurs as she turns to whisper to Tribbie, leaving Mydei fighting for his honor and Phainon nursing a purpling bruise on his ribs. 

The atmosphere remains light. It’s strange seeing how little Aglaea is bothered by this entire situation. If anything, she’s amused, lips curved upwards in a small but evident smile. The triplets are also at ease, laughing away and asking if they could pet Phainon’s fluffy ears to which Phainon, ever the gentleman, kneels down and allows them to pet him for as long as they want. Even Aglaea reaches out to pet Phainon’s ears, running gentle fingers through soft fur. 

This entire situation is odd. He almost wants to voice it, but there’s little use in bringing up the culprit. It’s less of a question of who did this—anyone with a working brain knows it’s Cipher—and more of, why? 

And knowing her, it’s probably because she felt like it. 

—𖤓—

There are tears in Cipher’s eyes. She takes one look and bursts into a fit of laughter.

Castorice gapes at him. Unable to say a word. With all due respect, she looks more akin to a fish out of water than a bunny. 

“What?” Mydei asks, crossing his arms tightly over his chest, a little defensive. 

“I thought—I really thought…” Cipher snorts. “Little lion—I mean cow. Little cow.” The edges of her lips tremble and she keels over, unable to hold in her laughter.

“Bull,” Mydei corrects. Even though he's grasping at straws. He’s clinging on like a particularly stubborn weed in an otherwise flourishing garden. 

It’s Castorice’s turn to snort. 

He turns to look at her, and she squeaks out, “Oops. Sorry…”

She doesn’t seem too sorry though—not with the way she immediately bursts into a fit of giggles alongside Cipher. They spur each other on. Cipher laughs loudly and Castorice laughs even louder. 

He’s stuck standing there, feeling like the odd one out. Cipher leans on a nearby pillar to catch her breath while Castorice has dramatically fallen to her knees, bunny ears twitching as she bunches the fabric of her dress. Her bangs cover her eyes as she tries and fails to hold back her giggles.  

Thankfully, Phainon isn’t here or else he’d join in this madness. With a small frown, Mydei reaches up to touch his ears and then his pitifully tiny horns.

In a daze, he walks off and nearly crashes into a wall or three. Cipher and Castorice don’t even try to stop him, both too inebriated off his misery. Sadists, the two of them. 

He’s a bull—not a cow. Why do people default to calling him a cow? It doesn’t make any sense. 

First of all, he’s never given birth before, so he’d be a heifer if anything. Second of all, he’s a man and that alone excludes him from being a cow. 

Male cattle are bulls, not cows. 

He’s sure being called a bull is an insult. Bull-headed. More bull than man. 

But the alternative is being a cow. Okay, in this case, maybe being a cow isn’t so bad then. At least he’d be spared the insults. 

In the back alley of some random Okheman street—he’s not sure where he is to be honest—Mydei squats on the ground and buries his head in his hands.

Titans hear his plea. He’s about to lose it. 

Why couldn’t he have been a lion? It’s what everyone had expected. Instead he’s rocking these spotted ears and tiny horns. 

Unfortunately for him and probably the rest of Okhema—barring the weirdos who are actually enjoying having new appendages—Cipher’s magic works outside the realm of reality. Anything could happen when it involves the demigod of trickery.

This must be rigged. There’s no way. 

And he doesn’t even want to begin on the weird slickness between his thighs every time something accident brushes against his tits—ahem, pecs—or if the Deliverer—infuriating as always—looks at him in that smiley, sunshine way of his. 

It’s not sweat, that’s for sure. Is this some strange biological change now that he’s a bovine? 

He’s not sure who he can even ask. Maybe Hyacine—who turns out to be yet another bunny—but he doesn’t wish to terrorize her with his strange, new bodily functions. She already has her hands full with the entirety of Okhema sprouting animal features overnight. 

He’s seen the line of people waiting outside her clinic. 

Poor Hyacine.

“Your highness!” a young recruit greets, horse ears flicking. His gaze trails down to Mydei’s chest. “You’re a… c—” 

“Bull,” Mydei supplies. He doesn’t even believe it anymore, but he says it either way. No one in Okhema believes him. Not even his countrymen. Anyone with eyes really. 

“Y-Yes!” the soldier coughs into his hand. “G-Glory to Castrum Kremnos!”

The man’s gaze remains hyper focused on Mydei’s chest. 

His impressive physique and crimson markings have always garnered attention, but now, he’s getting attention for an entirely different reason. 

It’s a few minutes later when another soldier, an older man whom Mydei has known for years, approaches and greets, “Hello, your highness.” Once again, as if his chest is a magnet, the man’s gaze lands on his heavy breast. 

Only this time… Oh titans. Mydei can’t even find himself to care that the man is gaping at his chest because the truth is staring him in the eye and whispering for him to admit defeat. He’s almost offended by how big and in his face it is. 

Those horns are thick and curved upwards, strong and shining with power. 

The man in front of him—there’s no mistaking it—is a bull. 

Full horns, not the little stubs that decorate Mydei’s head. His ears are dark brown, not at all white and spotted like Mydei’s. 

As crown prince and leader of the Kremnoan detachment, he can safely say that he’s never going to live this down. 

Okay, whatever. He’s a cow. He admits it! At least his chest hasn’t begun to leak milk…

He counts his blessings. 

—𖤓—

Their spars take on a new tone. No longer is it a match borne of two equals. Now, Phainon looks at him like he’s a meal. 

He supposes it’s true. After all, Phainon is an apex predator, a hungry wolf, while Mydei… well, he’s a cow—ahem, bull. He’s a bull… bovine… 

… It doesn’t matter anymore. 

Either way, still a herbivore. A grass eater. 

Prey. 

There’s that creep in the back of his head that won’t go away telling him to run, hide. He’s not safe out here. His movements are slower, less coordinated, and he’s sure Phainon has already noticed. His body reacts like he’s been tossed back into the sea of souls, on edge, tension bleeding into his movements like he’s a puppet on strings. 

What was once an enjoyable activity that left his body tingling all over has devolved into a struggle to keep himself calm. His ears flatten against his head when Phainon throws a particularly brutal kick that’s promptly blocked by the metal plates of his gauntlets. 

Those giant wolf ears flick and twitch, a distraction that Mydei is loath to admit affects him a little too much. Blue eyes are bright, the thrill of battle evident in his mused moonlight locks and the sheen of sweat beading on his brow.

And that tail… That fluffy white tail wagging back and forth. It started off slow. Now, it’s spinning like a propeller. 

There’s this newfound tension in the air. It’s like he’s moving through sludge, and it comes to no surprise when he’s thrown off balance and ends up tumbling onto the floor. 

His breaths come out ragged. His tail is being squashed by his ass, and it’s not a good feeling. He shifts to a better position. Also, his chest feels strange, tingly yet stuffy, but that’s a whole other ordeal to unpack. 

Phainon looms over him, a shadow cast over his brilliant features. He looks far more menacing like this, so much taller than Mydei, so much more threatening. 

Blue eyes flick downwards. “Mydei.” 

“What?” He braces himself for Phainon’s inevitable gloat. 

“Are your nipples leaking?” Phainon asks, gaze honed in like a sniper catching his target. Except the target are his aching nipples. 

It takes a little time for the words to register. Leaking…? 

No. They’re not leaking. Why would his nipples be leaking? What kind of question is that? 

Has the Deliverer finally lost all brain cells? He knew it was coming but not this soon.

Yes, his chest feels wet but that happens all the time after a spar. He’s merely sweating and nothing more—

Mydei stares down. 

For a moment, he’s unsure of what he’s looking at. Sweat isn’t translucent.

And then it registers. 

Oh titans. 

They’re leaking. His nipples are actually leaking.

Milky droplets bead from the hard nubs. It trails down the round of his breast in small rivulets. 

He doesn't know what to do. Scream like a banshee? Cover his chest like a flustered maiden? Run away and barricade himself in his house?

A whirlwind of options fly through his mind. His head spins. 

If this had been a real battle, he would have been dead. A moment of weakness that would have led to certain downfall—
